Linearizer of equations of motion

Source: R/physics-mechanics-linearize.R
Linearizer.Rd

Linearizer() holds the general form of a system's equations of motion and linearizes them about an operating point, as SymPy's Linearizer. It is usually made by the to_linearizer() method of KanesMethod() or LagrangesMethod(); linearize(op_point, A_and_B, simplify) (reached with $) returns M, A and B, or A and B.

Usage

Linearizer(
  f_0,
  f_1,
  f_2,
  f_3,
  f_4,
  f_c,
  f_v,
  f_a,
  q,
  u,
  q_i = NULL,
  q_d = NULL,
  u_i = NULL,
  u_d = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  lams = NULL,
  linear_solver = "LU"
)

Arguments

f_0, f_1, f_2, f_3, f_4, f_c, f_v, f_a

The matrices of the general form.

q, u

Generalized coordinates and speeds.

q_i, q_d, u_i, u_d

Independent and dependent coordinates and speeds.

r

Input variables.

lams

Lagrange multipliers.

linear_solver

"LU" or a function of A and b.

Value

A Linearizer object.

Examples

q <- dynamicsymbols("q"); u <- dynamicsymbols("u")
qd <- dynamicsymbols("q", 1); ud <- dynamicsymbols("u", 1)
k <- Symbol("k")
lin <- Linearizer(list(qd), list(-u), list(ud), list(k * q), list(0),
                  list(), list(), list(), list(q), list(u),
                  q_i = list(q), u_i = list(u))
lin$linearize(A_and_B = TRUE)
#> (Matrix([[0, 1], [-k, 0]]), Matrix(0, 0, []))
